e.body:
**AI Adoption in Finance**（Zenodo `10.5281/zenodo.22846879`，版本 `1.0.3`）**是一份**把**「**人**机**分歧**率」**本身**当**数据**发布**的**机构**投资者 **AI** 采用**语料****——**逐字自述**为**「**A public, sourced classification of where institutional investors sit on AI adoption — pensions, sovereign-wealth funds, endowments, asset managers and hedge funds — placed on a four-stage bar (exploring / piloting / scaling / embedded) from public evidence alone.**」**。**⭐ 本条目属于本轮主题**「**跨仓储聚合面**」**。
**可核实信息（均 2026-09-22 Zenodo 与 GitHub 接口实测）**：
**⭐⭐⭐ ① 它**把**人**机**分歧**率**当**数据**发布**，**并**立刻**限定**它**能**证明**什么****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**描述**逐字**写**「**An AI research agent drafts every row and proposes a stage; a human verifies every row against its cited sources before it publishes. Because each review decision is recorded, the rate at which the human and the agent disagree is published as data rather than asserted: see data/agreement.json. Those figures are anchored agreement and an upper bound on reproducibility, never an inter-rater reliability coefficient — the reviewer saw the proposed stage before deciding.**」**；**⭐ 本词条认为**这一处**对 **RIAA** 最有用**：**⭐ 即**「**人**工**复核**过 **AI **输出」**这**句话**在**多数**报告里**是**修辞**，**而**这**里**把**它**变**成**可**计算**的**量**，**并**明确**承认**「**复核**者**先**看**到**了**建议**答案」**——**⭐ 对**写**「**AI** 辅助**流程」**章节**的人**：**「**谁**先**看**到**什么」**决定**了**这个**数字**能**不**能**叫**「**评分**者**一致**性」**；**⭐ 而**这**一**点**在**方法**章节**里**极**常**被**含**糊**过**去**。
**⭐⭐ ② 它**把**「**没**能**分类」**的**机构**也**具名**列**出**，**从**而**给**出**分母****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**描述**逐字**写**「**Institutions assessed against the methodology whose public record did not support a stage are published by name with reasons in data/not_classified.json, so the corpus can be read as a rate rather than a highlight reel.**」**；**⭐ 本词条**据此**指出**：**⭐ 即**只**列**「**已**采用 **AI」**的**机构**，**读者**会**把**名单**当**成**趋势**；**列**出**「**够**不**上**标准**者」**并**给**理由**，**读者**才**能**算**比例**（**⭐ 与**第 **378** 轮**记下的**「**样本** vs **全量**要**标注」**同**一**脉络，**第 **379** 轮**的**是**「**合成** vs **真实」**，**这**一**次**是**「**分母**在**哪」）**；**⭐ 对 RIAA**：**做**名单**式**研究**（**哪**些**公司**做**了**什么）**时**，**把**「**检查**过**但**不**符合**标准」**的**一并**列**出**，**成本**很**低**、**说服**力**很**大**。
**⭐⭐ ③ 它**逐字**声明**覆盖率**不**是**任何**总体**的**样本**，**故**数字**不**得**当**行业**比例****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**描述**逐字**写**「**Coverage is not a sample of any defined population — institutions enter through research passes, not a sampling frame — so every figure describes this corpus and none is an industry rate.**」**；**⭐ 本词条认为**这一句**是**本条**价值**最高**的**一**处**：**⭐ 即**它**主**动**切断**了**「**我**的**数据** → **行业**结论」**这**条**最**常见**的**误**用**路径**；**⭐ 对 RIAA**：**引**用**任何**非**抽样**数据**（**包括**本站**这类**「**检索**发现」**的**语料）**时**，**都**要**写**一**句**「**这**是**语料**，**不**是**样本」**。
**⭐⭐ ④ 它**有**一**整**段**独立性**与**利益**声明**，**并**把**关**联**机构**排除**在**覆盖**外****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**描述**逐字**含**「**Independence. This is an independent personal project, produced entirely in the author’s personal capacity. It is not affiliated with, sponsored by, funded by, or endorsed by any employer or institution, and every view and classification in it is the author’s alone. No non-public information from the author’s professional work informs any classification, and institutions where the author has a professional affiliation are excluded from coverage entirely. Nothing here is investment advice.**」**；**⭐ 本词条**据此**指出**：**⭐ 即**「**排除**与**作者**有**职业**关联**的**机构」**这**条**做法**比**单纯**声明**「**我**很**客观」**强**，**因**为**它**是**可**核对**的**（**读者**可以**去**名单里**找**有**没有**那**家**机构）**；**⭐ 对 RIAA**：**写**独立**研究**声明**时**，**给出**一条**可**核对**的**排除**规则**，**而**不**只**是**一句**保证**。
**⭐⭐ ⑤ 许可**分**两**层**与**引用**口径****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**描述**逐字**写**「**Licensing: the data files in data/ are CC BY 4.0; the code in this repository is MIT. This record is registered under CC BY 4.0 because the corpus is the citable artifact.**」**；**⭐ 记录**侧**许可**逐字 **`cc-by-4.0`**、**访问**逐字 **`open`****；**⭐ 本词条**据此**指出**：**⭐ 即**「**数**据**与**代码**许可**不同」**是**本轮／上轮**反复**出现**的**形态**（**⭐ 第 **379** 轮**的**西班牙**养老金**包**与**本轮**两**条 **JOSS** 工件**同**属**此**类）**，**而**它**还**逐字**说明**「**为何**记录**用 **CC BY**：**因**为**语料**才**是**可**引用**的**工件」**。
**⭐⭐ ⑥ 元数据**与**窗口****——**⭐ 本次实测**：**发布日 **2026-09-19****（**窗口内）**、**版本逐字 **`1.0.3`****、**作者逐字 **`Ma, Jiajun`****、**文件**逐字 **`jima1835/ai-adoption-in-finance-v1.0.3.zip`（**798,220 B）**、**相关**标识**逐字 **`isSupplementTo` 指向 **GitHub** 的 **`github.com/jima1835/ai-adoption-in-finance/tree/v1.0.3`****；**⭐ 仓库**逐字 **★3、**MIT、**主**语言 **JavaScript、**仓库 **977 KB、**创建 **2026-06-07、**末次**推送 **2026-09-19****；**⭐ 本词条**如实**指出**：**⭐ 即 **★3** 与**较**小**体量**说明**它**是**个人**项目**（**⭐ 而**其**描述**也**逐字**自称 **`an independent personal project`）**，**故**「**能**不**能**长期**维护」**要**自行**判断**。
**⭐⭐ ⑦ 与池内条目的关系**：**本站 [[finproof-bench]] 覆盖**金融 **AI** 护栏**基准**、**[[ai-agents-for-insurance-guide]] 覆盖**保险**业 **AI** 智能体**落地**、**[[insurance-ai-reliability-benchmark]] 覆盖**保险 **AI** 可靠性**基准**——**⭐ 而**本条补上的是**「**把**人**机**分歧**率**与**未**分类**名单**一并**发布**的**机构**采用**语料」这一**形态**；**⭐ 本词条**不对以上任何一条做代码级比较**。
**对 RIAA**：**⭐ 五件事值得借**：**① **人**工**复核**要**给出**可**计算**的**分歧**量**，**并**说明**复核**者**看到**了**什么**；**② **名**单**研究**要**给**分母**（**未**达标**者**也**列出**并**给**理由）**；**③ **非**抽样**语料**要**声明**「**不**是**行业**比例」**；**④ **独立**性**声明**要**含**可**核对**的**排除**规则**；**⑤ **记录**与**数据**、**代码**的**许可**分开**标注**。
**⚠️ 本词条如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次**没有下载**其 **zip**（**798,220 B）**、**未读**其 **`data/agreement.json`** 与 **`data/not_classified.json`** 的**内容**、**未**核对**其**任何**一条**机构**分类**，**故**不**主张**其**分类**准确性**、**方法**可靠性**或**覆盖**完整性**。**② ⚠️ 本次**只读 **Zenodo** 记录**接口**返回的**元数据与描述**（**描述**实测 **1,912** 字符）**与 **GitHub** 仓库**接口**，**未读**其**代码**或**数据**文件**。**③ ⚠️ **未核实**其**「**四**阶段**」**（**exploring／**piloting／**scaling／**embedded）**的**判定**规则**。**④ ⚠️ **未核实**其**覆盖**的**机构**数量**（**描述**未**给出**总数，**本词条**也**不**推断）**。**⑤ ⚠️ **未核实**其 **`isSupplementTo`** 指向**的 **GitHub** 版本**与**存档**内容**是否**一致**。**⑥ ⚠️ **★3** 为 **2026-09-22** 快照**。**⑦ ⚠️ 窗口**状况**：**发布日 **2026-09-19** 与**仓库**末次**推送 **2026-09-19** 均**落在**本轮**窗口**之内**（**基准日 **2026-09-22）**。**⑧ ⚠️ 本条目**所记为 **2026-09-22 所见**；**⚠️ 涉及**机构**投资**者**与 **AI** 采用**，**⚠️ 不**构成**任何**投资**建议**（**⭐ 其**描述**亦逐字**声明 **`Nothing here is investment advice.`）**。

e.title_en: A corpus of institutional investor AI adoption that publishes the rate at which a human reviewer and an AI agent disagree as data rather than as an assertion, while explicitly limiting what that number means: the record states that the figures are anchored agreement and an upper bound on reproducibility and never an inter-rater reliability coefficient, because the reviewer saw the proposed stage before deciding; institutions whose public record did not support a stage are published by name with reasons, so the corpus can be read as a rate rather than a highlight reel; and the record states that coverage is not a sample of any defined population, so every figure describes the corpus and none is an industry rate.

e.summary_en: This is a corpus of institutional investor AI adoption that publishes the rate at which a human reviewer and an AI agent disagree as data rather than as an assertion. **Measured this round**: released on the nineteenth of September inside the window, typed as a dataset, licensed for attribution use, openly accessible, credited to one author, and shipped as a single archive of about eight hundred kilobytes, while the companion repository shows a small star count, an MIT licence, one language, a repository of about one megabyte, creation in June, and a push inside the window. **This entry belongs to the round theme of cross-repository metadata aggregation.** **Four things are worth reading: it publishes the human-agent disagreement rate as data and immediately limits what that number can prove, stating that the figures are anchored agreement and an upper bound on reproducibility and never an inter-rater reliability coefficient, because the reviewer saw the proposed stage before deciding, which is the classic bias of grading a paper after seeing the answer key; it publishes the institutions that could not be classified by name with reasons, so that a reader with a denominator can read the list as a rate rather than a highlight reel, the same line as the earlier sample-versus-full-data note but with the ones below the bar as the denominator; it states in writing that coverage is not a sample of any defined population and that every figure describes the corpus rather than an industry rate, so its numbers cannot be quoted as sector statistics; and it carries a full independence statement, including the exclusion of any institution where the author has a professional affiliation and a closing note that nothing in it is investment advice.** **No archive was downloaded and no single classification was checked this round.**

e.body_en:
This is a corpus of institutional investor AI adoption that publishes the rate at which a human reviewer and an AI agent disagree as data rather than as an assertion. **This entry belongs to the round theme of cross-repository metadata aggregation.**
**Verified information, all measured on 2026-09-22 from the Zenodo and repository interfaces**:
**First, it publishes the human-agent disagreement rate as data and immediately limits what that number can prove.** The record states that an AI research agent drafts every row and proposes a stage, that a human verifies every row against its cited sources before publication, that because each review decision is recorded the disagreement rate is published as data rather than asserted, and then that those figures are anchored agreement and an upper bound on reproducibility and never an inter-rater reliability coefficient, because the reviewer saw the proposed stage before deciding. **A claim that a human reviewed AI output is rhetoric in most reports, whereas here it becomes a computable quantity with an explicit admission that the reviewer saw the proposed answer first, which is the classic bias of grading after seeing the answer key. Anyone writing an AI-assisted workflow section should ask who saw what first, because that determines whether the number may be called inter-rater agreement at all, and this is precisely the point that methods sections usually blur.**
**Second, it publishes the institutions that could not be classified by name, which supplies the denominator.** The record states that institutions assessed against the methodology whose public record did not support a stage are published by name with reasons, so the corpus can be read as a rate rather than a highlight reel. **Listing only the institutions that adopted AI invites the reader to read a trend, while listing the ones that fell short together with reasons lets the reader compute a proportion, which is the same line as the earlier note that a sample must be labelled as such, and as the later note that a synthetic file must be distinguished from real data, with the denominator being the question this time.**
**Third, it states in writing that coverage is not a sample of any defined population, so its figures cannot be quoted as industry rates.** The record says that institutions enter through research passes rather than a sampling frame, and that every figure describes the corpus and none is an industry rate. **That sentence deliberately cuts the most common misuse path, from my data to a sector conclusion, and it generalises: any non-sampled corpus, including the kind of discovery-based collection kept on this site, should carry a sentence saying it is a corpus and not a sample.**
**Fourth, it carries a full independence statement and excludes affiliated institutions from coverage.** The record states that the work is an independent personal project produced entirely in the author personal capacity, that it is not affiliated with, sponsored by, funded by, or endorsed by any employer or institution, that no non-public information from professional work informs any classification, that institutions where the author has a professional affiliation are excluded from coverage entirely, and that nothing in it is investment advice. **An exclusion rule that a reader can check against the list is stronger than a general assurance of objectivity, and writing an independence statement with one checkable exclusion rule is the transferable practice.**
**Fifth, licensing is split by layer and the citation rationale is stated.** The record says that the data files are under one attribution licence and the code under a permissive licence, and that the record is registered under the attribution licence because the corpus is the citable artefact, with the record itself typed as a dataset, openly accessible, and licensed accordingly. **Data and code carrying different licences has now recurred across rounds, and this record goes further by explaining why the record uses the licence it does.**
**Sixth, metadata and window status.** Released on the nineteenth of September inside the window at a patch version, credited to one author, shipping as an archive of about eight hundred kilobytes and linked by a supplement relation to a tagged repository version, while the repository shows a small star count, an MIT licence, one language, a repository of about one megabyte, creation in June, and a push inside the window. **The small star count and size mark it as a personal project, which its own description states in writing, so whether it will be maintained is a judgement for the reader.**
**Seventh, relative to existing entries**: pooled entries cover a financial AI guardrail benchmark, a guide to AI agents in insurance, and an insurance AI reliability benchmark, **while this entry supplies the form of an institutional adoption corpus that publishes both the human-agent disagreement rate and the unclassified list. This entry makes no code-level comparison against any of them.**
**For RIAA**: **five practices transfer: give a computable disagreement figure for human review and say what the reviewer saw; give a denominator in list-based research by publishing those that fell short, with reasons; state that a non-sampled corpus is not an industry rate; include a checkable exclusion rule in independence statements; and label licences separately for data, code, and the record.**
**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, no archive was downloaded, the agreement and unclassified files were not read, and no single classification was checked**, so no claim is made about classification accuracy, methodological reliability, or coverage completeness. **Second, only the metadata and description, measured at about nineteen hundred characters, and the repository interface were read**, not the code or the data files. **Third, the four-stage decision rules and the number of institutions covered were not verified**, the description giving no total and this entry inferring none. **Fourth, whether the tagged repository version matches the archive contents was not verified. Fifth, the star count is a snapshot from the twenty-second of September. Sixth, the release and the repository push both fall inside this round window against that baseline. Seventh, this entry records what was visible on that date and states plainly that it constitutes no investment advice, as the record itself also states in writing.**
e.body_hk:
**AI Adoption in Finance**（Zenodo `10.5281/zenodo.22846879`，版本 `1.0.3`）**是一份**把**「**人機分歧率」**本身**當數據**發布**的機構投資者 **AI 採用語料****——**逐字自述**為**「**A public, sourced classification of where institutional investors sit on AI adoption — pensions, sovereign-wealth funds, endowments, asset managers and hedge funds — placed on a four-stage bar (exploring / piloting / scaling / embedded) from public evidence alone.**」**。**⭐ 本條目屬於本輪主題**「**跨倉儲聚合面**」**。
**可核實資訊（均 2026-09-22 Zenodo 與 GitHub 介面實測）**：
**⭐⭐⭐ ① 把人機分歧率當數據發布並立刻限定它能證明什麼**——**逐字**Because each review decision is recorded, the rate at which the human and the agent disagree is published as data rather than asserted: see data/agreement.json. Those figures are anchored agreement and an upper bound on reproducibility, never an inter-rater reliability coefficient — the reviewer saw the proposed stage before deciding.**；**⭐ 即**人工複核這句話被拆成可計算的量**，**並承認複核者先看到建議答案**——**⭐ 即**「**知道答案再判卷」**的經典偏誤**。
**⭐⭐ ② 把沒能分類的機構具名列出（**`data/not_classified.json`）**——**逐字**so the corpus can be read as a rate rather than a highlight reel.**；**⭐ 即**只列已採用者會被讀成趨勢**，**列出夠不上標準者才能算比例**。
**⭐⭐ ③ 逐字聲明覆盖率不是任何總體的樣本**——**逐字**Coverage is not a sample of any defined population — institutions enter through research passes, not a sampling frame — so every figure describes this corpus and none is an industry rate.**；**⭐ 即**主動切斷「**我的數據→**行業結論」**這條誤用路徑**。
**⭐⭐ ④ 一整段獨立性聲明並排除關聯機構**——**逐字**This is an independent personal project, produced entirely in the author’s personal capacity. It is not affiliated with, sponsored by, funded by, or endorsed by any employer or institution, and every view and classification in it is the author’s alone. No non-public information from the author’s professional work informs any classification, and institutions where the author has a professional affiliation are excluded from coverage entirely. Nothing here is investment advice.**；**⭐ 即**排除規則可核對**，**比單純聲明客觀更強**。
**⭐⭐ ⑤ 許可分兩層與引用口徑**——**逐字**the data files in data/ are CC BY 4.0; the code in this repository is MIT. This record is registered under CC BY 4.0 because the corpus is the citable artifact.**。
**⭐⭐ ⑥ 元數據與窗口**——**發布日 2026-09-19**、**版本 `1.0.3`**、**作者 `Ma, Jiajun`**、**文件 798,220 B**、**相關標識 `isSupplementTo` 指向 GitHub `github.com/jima1835/ai-adoption-in-finance/tree/v1.0.3`**；**倉庫逐字 ★3、**MIT、**JavaScript、**977 KB、**創建 2026-06-07、**末次推送 2026-09-19**。
**⭐⭐ ⑦ 與池內條目的關係**：[[finproof-bench]]、[[ai-agents-for-insurance-guide]]、[[insurance-ai-reliability-benchmark]]——**⭐ 本條補上的是**「**把人機分歧率與未分類名單一併發布的機構採用語料**」**這一形態**。
**對 RIAA**：**⭐ 五件事值得借**：**① **複核要給可計算的分歧量與看到什麼**；**② **名單研究要給分母**；**③ **非抽樣語料要聲明不是行業比例**；**④ **獨立性聲明要含可核對的排除規則**；**⑤ **許可分別標註**。
**⚠️ 本詞條如實標註**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次**沒有下載其 zip、**未讀 agreement.json 與 not_classified.json 內容、**未核對任何一條分類**，**不主張其分類準確性、**方法可靠性或**覆蓋完整性**。**② ⚠️ 本次**只讀元資料與描述（**實測 1,912 字符）與**GitHub 介面**，**未讀其代碼或數據文件**。**③ ⚠️ **未核實**四階段判定規則與**覆蓋機構數量**（**描述未給總數，**本條不推斷**）**。**④ ⚠️ **未核實**其 GitHub 版本與存檔內容是否一致**。**⑤ ⚠️ **★3 為 2026-09-22 快照**。**⑥ ⚠️ 窗口狀況：**發布日與末次推送 2026-09-19 均在本輪窗口之內（**基準日 2026-09-22）**。**⑦ ⚠️ 本條目所記為 2026-09-22 所見**；**⚠️ 不構成任何投資建議**（**其描述亦逐字聲明 Nothing here is investment advice.**）**。
